headline: Revenue steady, margins compress on new-property costs
summary_short: Q2 revenue was essentially flat y/y at $1,034.4M (+3.7% q/q) as gaming growth was offset by lost market-access fees; net income fell 13.4% y/y to $131.2M on higher new-property depreciation, while EPS of $1.75 rose 27.7% q/q on lower interest expense and a smaller share count.
summary_long: Revenue was $1,034.4M, flat y/y (+0.04%) and +3.7% q/q: a 1.8% rise in gaming revenue plus Boyd Interactive and Sky River management-fee growth were largely offset by market-access fee terminations tied to the FanDuel Equity Sale. Operating income fell 17.2% y/y to $200.7M on higher depreciation from newly opened properties (Norfolk, Cadence Crossing) and higher preopening/writedown costs. Net income fell 13.4% y/y to $131.2M, cushioned by a $19.2M drop in interest expense after FanDuel-sale proceeds retired $1.68B of debt; EPS was $1.75 (-4.9% y/y, +27.7% q/q), helped by a 9.1% smaller diluted share count from buybacks. FY2026 total capex guided to $650-700M, including $300M for Norfolk. Cash $322.7M; Q2 dividend $0.20/share, buybacks $156.0M.

drivers.explanation: Gaming revenue +1.8% (slot win +2.4%, slot handle +1.6%) plus Boyd Interactive and Sky River management-fee growth were offset by market-access fee terminations tied to the FanDuel Equity Sale and lower online reimbursements.

Higher depreciation from newly opened properties (Norfolk transitional casino, Cadence Crossing) and higher project development/preopening/writedown costs, plus the loss of high-margin market-access fee revenue.
Tracks the decline in operating income, partially offset by a $19.2M y/y drop in interest expense after FanDuel Equity Sale proceeds retired $1.68B of Prior Credit Facility debt in Q3 2025.
EPS fell less than net income (-4.9% vs -13.4% y/y) because weighted diluted shares outstanding were 9.1% lower y/y, reflecting the buyback program retiring shares.

Company reiterated a FY2026 total capital-spending plan of $650-700M, including $300M toward the $750M Norfolk resort project and $75M for hotel renovations, funded from cash on hand and the Credit Facility.
